en: The Legend of the Elder Tālavaṇṭadāyaka The Seventh [Legend] in the Hatthivagga of the Therāpadāna I gave a palm-leaf fan to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was seated beneath a tree. Because of that root of merit, I have now attained the fruit of Arhatship. May I never again be born into a state of woe. “A palm-leaf fan was given by me to Tissa,
the kinsman of the Sun,
for the purpose of cooling him in the summer heat.”
For the sake of the pacification of feverish distress,
I extinguish the fire of lust and,
beyond that, the fire of hatred.
I have extinguished the fire of delusion;
this is the fruit of the palm-leaf fan.
My defilements have been burnt away.
All states of existence have been utterly eradicated;
I bear my final body in the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One.
In the ninety-two aeons since then,
because of the deed I performed back then,
I have not known a miserable rebirth.
This is the fruit of a palm-leaf fan.
In the sixty-third aeon from now,
one named Mahānāma—
Endowed with the seven treasures,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power;
the four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Tālavaṇṭadāyaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Tālavaṇṭadāyaka is the seventh.
